newsitem.title: INDIA: Merrill shifts Latin American funds into India.
newsitem.headline: Merrill shifts Latin American funds into India.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch said on Friday it was moving funds into Indian stock markets from Latin America.
Merrill said the performance of Indian equities during the next six to nine months could surprise investors, in a strategy report titled "As We See It: India on Full Throttle".
"We are moving funds into the market at the expense of Latin America," Merrill said.
"Regionally, we think Korea and Thailand will be important stories going out a year, but there may be a near-term opportunity cost of not exploiting the Indian story."

Merrill said falling interest rates and the likelihood that the 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget would emerge unscathed from the recent political crisis were both likely to result in healthy economic growth.
"We are taking the funds from Latin America, recognising the strong regional performance we have seen," Merrill said.
"This does not represent a major strategic shift, rather a fine-tuning. India is only about one-fourth the size of Latin America in terms of market capitalisation."
Merrill said price-to-earnings multiples of Indian stocks had bounced back from lows hit at the end of calendar 1996, but the market had a long way to go before it looked "extended."
"India appears to offer some of the best value regionally. We see little downside risk from here on a strategic view."
The U.S. firm said Korea and Thailand had been major regional commitments in its portfolio strategy.
"But there may be near-term performance challenges in those markets until we begin to see the sort of positive fundamental surprises we expect later this year," Merrill said without elaborating.
"We find India to be a perfectly reasonable place to park money at this point in time."
